intro: Pagination returns both a subset and enough metadata to navigate the rest. A caller should not have to infer whether another page exists from a full-looking final page.
task: Return an offset page together with total count and the next offset.
requirements: offset is integer 0..1e9 and limit integer 1..1000. Return items slice, total count, and next_offset when more items remain; otherwise next_offset is None. An offset beyond the end gives an empty page.

Sequence inputs are Python lists or tuples of at most 1000 items. Text inputs contain valid Unicode scalar characters and at most 10000 characters. Identifier and dictionary keys are nonempty strings of at most 100 characters. Numeric values are finite Python ints or floats with magnitude at most 1e9; bool is not numeric. Integer inputs must be Python ints, excluding bool, within the task-specific bounds or -1e9..1e9 when no narrower bounds are stated. Plain record data may contain strings, numbers, booleans, None, lists, tuples, and dictionaries; nesting is limited to six levels and dictionaries to 1000 keys.
Return the documented Python output types and preserve all caller inputs. Raise ValueError for invalid inputs unless the task explicitly reports a record-level rejection.

hints.title: Trace one record
hints.body: The total count describes the full collection, not the current page.

hints.title: Handle the boundary
hints.body: A next offset exists only if the end of this page is strictly before the collection end.

explanation: Pagination returns both a subset and enough metadata to navigate the rest. A caller should not have to infer whether another page exists from a full-looking final page.
This contract operates on a fixed in-memory snapshot. Real mutable datasets may need cursor semantics, but offset boundaries are useful to understand before adding that complexity.
